rules.statement: A daughter dowried by her brother is debarred from the inheritance under the Tesawalamai, even if the dowry was given out of property belonging to the brother and his wife.
rules.supporting_quote: "The important point is that the Code puts an obligation on the mother to dowry daughters. It does not say, nor can one assume, that the mother has to dowry a daughter from her own share, leaving intact that daughter's share inherited from her father. The admitted principle of the Tesawalamai is 'that if a daughter is dowried she loses her rights to her parents' inheritance, and section 9 is intended to carry this principle into effect after the father has died.'"
